paragraphs: The AMG GT R uses the M178 — a 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 that was fitted to the C190 generation from 2015 to 2023. It's the most track-focused version of the first‑generation AMG GT, and its engine shares the same core design as other M178‑powered variants. The AMG GT R is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every AMG GT R on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the AMG GT R from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the GT R uses a single engine code (M178) across its entire C190 run, there's less guesswork than with some multi-engine models. However, the M178 appeared in different states of tune across the AMG GT range, and ancillaries (turbochargers, cooling systems, ECU calibration) vary by sub‑variant. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm: - Your exact M178 engine code and generation - Specific GT R tuning and component spec - Any unique parts fitted to the R version (e.g. different turbos or cooling) - ECU and drivetrain configuration
